classification.difficultyReason: Draw simple integer combinations of two perpendicular unit vectors on a supplied grid.

content.prompt: On the diagram, show position vectors representing:

spec.description: Six-by-six square grid with two given perpendicular unit vectors. The labelled arrows prevent use of the blank-grid template.
spec.mathematics: The grid extends from -3 to 3 in both directions, with step 1. Vector a is (1,0), and vector b is (0,1).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two given unit arrows are visible.

answer.short: Arrow from the origin to two squares right and three squares up, labelled $2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b}$.
answer.worked: From the origin, move two squares right and three squares up. Draw an arrow from the origin to this endpoint and label it $2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b}$.

answer.short: Arrow from the origin to three squares right and one square down, labelled $3\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$.
answer.worked: From the origin, move three squares right and one square down. Draw an arrow from the origin to this endpoint and label it $3\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$.

answer.short: Arrow from the origin to two squares left and two squares down, labelled $-2\underset{\sim}{a}-2\underset{\sim}{b}$.
answer.worked: From the origin, move two squares left and two squares down. Draw an arrow from the origin to this endpoint and label it $-2\underset{\sim}{a}-2\underset{\sim}{b}$.

spec.description: Complete shared answer grid with both given unit vectors and all three labelled resultant arrows.
spec.mathematics: All resultant arrows begin at (0,0); endpoints are (2,3), (3,-1) and (-2,-2). Grid step is 1.
